questions.q: The Newton-Raphson iteration formula is:
questions.explain: Newton-Raphson: x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n).

questions.q: For x_{n+1} = (x_n + 6)^(1/2) with x_0 = 3, x_1 equals:
questions.explain: x_1 = sqrt(3 + 6) = sqrt(9) = 3 (a fixed point).

questions.q: Increasing the number of strips in the trapezium rule generally makes the estimate:
questions.explain: More (thinner) strips reduce the error, improving accuracy.

questions.q: A fixed point of the iteration x_{n+1} = g(x_n) satisfies:
questions.explain: At a fixed point the value is unchanged, so x = g(x), which solves the rearranged equation.

questions.q: Fixed-point iteration x_{n+1} = g(x_n) converges near a root when:
questions.explain: Convergence requires the magnitude of the derivative of g at the root to be less than 1.

questions.q: If f(a) and f(b) have the same sign, the sign-change test:
options: proves there is no root in (a,b)
questions.explain: No sign change means the test gives no information; roots may still exist (e.g. an even number).

questions.q: An iterative method has the form:
questions.explain: Fixed-point iteration repeatedly applies x_{n+1} = g(x_n).

questions.q: For numerical integration with the trapezium rule using ordinates y0...yn and strip width h, the estimate is:
questions.explain: Trapezium rule: (h/2)[(end ordinates) + 2×(sum of interior ordinates)].

questions.q: The bisection method repeatedly halves an interval, keeping the half where f:
questions.explain: Bisection retains the subinterval across which f changes sign.

questions.q: Using the trapezium rule on a concave-up region produces an estimate that is:
questions.explain: For a convex (concave-up) curve, trapezia lie above the curve, so the estimate is too large.

questions.q: The sign-change method locates a root by finding an interval where f(x):
questions.explain: A root lies where a continuous f changes sign across an interval.

questions.q: Newton-Raphson can fail if, at the iterate, f'(x_n) is:
questions.explain: If f'(x_n) = 0 the formula divides by zero (the tangent is horizontal), so the method fails.

questions.q: On a region where the curve is concave down, the trapezium rule:
questions.explain: For a concave-down curve the trapezia lie below the curve, underestimating the area.

questions.q: A 'staircase' pattern on a cobweb/staircase diagram indicates the iteration is:
questions.explain: A staircase pattern that closes in on the intersection shows monotonic convergence.

questions.q: A cobweb diagram that spirals outward from the root indicates:
questions.explain: An outward-spiralling cobweb shows the iteration diverges (|g'| > 1).

questions.q: To improve a root estimate found by sign change to greater accuracy, you can:
options: apply an iterative method or bisection
questions.explain: Refining with iteration, bisection, or Newton-Raphson narrows the root location.

questions.q: For f(x) = x^3 - x - 1, f(1) = -1 and f(2) = 5 show a root lies in:
questions.explain: f changes sign between 1 and 2, so a root lies in (1,2).
